subject: Deep-history latency flare: MediQ p99 spike during extended-session tests
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@mediq.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@mediq.com
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: High P99 for long-history sessions this morning

Ben —

We observed a sharp increase in p99 latency on Hosted API between 08:40–09:05 ET this morning during our automated end-to-end tests. The failures and spikes are concentrated on requests with extended session history (~30k tokens). Sample: request_id=mediq:20260722:rq-9c1b, p95=1.2s, p99=12.8s, error_rate up ~4x.

We collected a sample payload and the stack traces; attaching the bundle. This is blocking our production rollout for the new patient-handoff feature. Please advise immediate mitigation and ETA for a fix.

Thanks,
Tom
Operations, MediQ Health

Attachments: diagnostics_20260722.tar.gz, sample_request_32k.json

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@mediq.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2026 09:28:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: High P99 for long-history sessions this morning

Tom — thanks for the quick heads-up and the artifacts. We see the same spikes in our edge metrics for your tenant.

Immediate steps I'm initiating:
- Rate-limit large contexts from your API key for a short window (rolling 15m) to protect overall cluster health.
- Spin up a temporary fallback variant (quantized 16k-optimized) and wire routing for your tenant so extended sessions can be served with lower p99.
- Handing traces to runtime + SRE for a root-cause sweep (laura & vivek cc'd).

Could you confirm the acceptable degradation window and whether you want us to proceed with the fallback routing now? We can also queue a quick customer call in 30–45m.

—Ben
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, Tom Ellis <t.ellis@mediq.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2026 09:46:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: High P99 for long-history sessions this morning

Adding engineering context. Initial hypothesis based on traces: when we reconstruct KV cache for very long histories (>>16k) we're seeing repeated cache misses and a sustained spike in decode path CPU due to large attention windows. Two things to validate quickly:

1) Are the offending requests single large prompts or many concatenated session turns? (Tom: sample_request_32k looks like concatenated turns.)
2) Check whether your tenant was routed to a shard where quantization fallback happened — that increases token-cost and can spike latency under load.

What we'll do in parallel:
- Collect per-request cache-hit metrics and the exact model variant used for the sample requests.
- Run a synthetic replay against a reserved node with tracing enabled to reproduce p95/p99.

If we can reproduce, we should have a mitigation path (routing to the 16k-optimized variant) within the hour. For long-term fix, runtime will need a kernel/caching change to avoid repeated KV flushes for hybrid-history patterns.

Laura
Head of Runtime Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, Tom Ellis <t.ellis@mediq.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: High P99 for long-history sessions this morning

Quick notes from SRE/runtime:
- We've seen similar patterns on a canary last month where prefix caching policy caused degraded p99 for sessions with many short-turn messages (high prefix churn).
- I'll pull the batcher logs and the compile-time kernel selection logs to see if nodes fell back to a slower execution path.
- If fallback quantized kernels triggered under memory pressure, that would explain the sudden p99 delta (and the modest p95 impact).

Ben — please apply the temporary routing and also enable the dev-playback on a reserved node (I need the request_id).

Vivek
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@mediq.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2026 10:18:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: High P99 for long-history sessions this morning

Tom — we started the temporary protective measures at 10:12 ET:
- Short-term rate limit: large-context (>20k tokens) requests limited to 1rps per API key.
- Fallback routing: your key now routes extended sessions to a 16k-optimized quantized variant.
- We've queued a reserved node replay for the sample request (rq-9c1b) and provided it to SRE.

Expectations: these actions should bring p99 back under 3s for most requests; p95 should be unaffected or slightly better. I'll keep you updated at the 30m mark. For credits/contract impact, I'm looping in Neha from CS.

—Ben

From: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@mediq.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@mediq.com
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2026 10:31:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: High P99 for long-history sessions this morning

Thanks for the quick response and the mitigation. We agree to the temporary routing for now. Two asks:
1) Can you confirm the expected timeline for the full root-cause patch? Our launch is scheduled next week and we need confidence.
2) Given the production impact, we'd like to discuss a one-time service credit.

I'll standby for the 30m update.

—Tom

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, Tom Ellis <t.ellis@mediq.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2026 16:47:00 -04:00
Subject: Summary & next steps — MediQ deep-history p99 flare

Executive summary for internal owners + MediQ:
- Incident: p99 latency spike (to ~13s) observed 08:40–09:05 ET for extended-history requests (~30k tokens). Trigger appears to be repeated KV cache misses combined with quantization fallback on a subset of nodes under memory pressure.
- Mitigation applied: temporary rate limit (>20k tokens) + routing to 16k-optimized variant (applied 10:12 ET). Early metrics show p99 reduced to ~2.6s for most replayed samples; error rate recovered to baseline.
- Next steps (owners):
  * SRE (Vivek) — complete kernel selection and batcher log analysis; confirm whether we hit a specific fallback heuristic and propose immediate config change (ETA 24h).
  * Runtime (Laura) — prototype cache policy change to reduce repeated KV flushes on hybrid-history patterns; evaluate patch on reserved canary (ETA 72h).
  * CS/Finance (Neha) — handle MediQ credit request and customer comms; propose language and credit amount (ETA 24h).
  * Account (Ben) — coordinate postmortem and customer exec call; confirm MediQ launch implications and mitigation acceptance.

Tom — thanks again for rapid reporting and the artifacts. We'll follow up with a postmortem and a timeline for the permanent fix.

Attachments: p99_traces.txt

—Ben
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
